title: Ganza potato (NSIC Po 07): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Ganza potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Ganza potato is a potato variety from BSU NPRCRTC. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Ganza is a registered potato variety, also sold or known as NSIC Po 07. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2004 as NSIC 2004 Po 07. It comes from BSU NPRCRTC. Its record notes 19.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Ganza potato is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Po 07, this is the same potato. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [potato variety finder](/crop-varieties/potato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items: **Yield:** 19.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 19.68 t/ha trails the average of its group, 21.79. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [late blight](/diseases/late-blight).

The pests and diseases that hit potato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have light yellow flesh and cream skin. Dry matter is 17.18 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Light yellow flesh, cream skin, oblong oval tubers, dry matter about 17 percent.
**Where:** Hilly highland areas with fertile, moist soil.
Moderately resistant to late blight and peach scale insect.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a BSU table potato used as one of the check varieties in Benguet trials. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Ganza potato

Potato grows in the cool highlands of Benguet, Mountain Province and Bukidnon. Plant clean seed tubers, and pick a variety rated against late blight for the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Po 07 the same as Ganza?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Po 07 is another name for Ganza, registered as NSIC 2004 Po 07. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 19.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Ganza?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
